question: I transferred between two designated learning institutions. Can I still get a PGWP if my studies added up to at least 8 months?
answer:
Yes, you can still get a PGWP if your studies added up to at least 8 months. According to the sources:

(1) Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html
"If you transferred between designated learning institutions (DLIs)
The length of your studies must be at least 8 months for you to be eligible."

(1) Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html
"If you transferred from a non-DLI to a DLI
Only the time you spent studying at the DLI will be counted. You must spend at least 8 months at the DLI to be eligible for a PGWP."

So, as long as the total length of your studies is at least 8 months, you should be eligible for a PGWP.

question: Can I pay my restoration fees with a credit card that isn't in my name?
answer:
Yes, you can pay your restoration fees with a credit card that isn't in your name. (Source: [2] Extend your study permit or restore your status: How to apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/extend-study-permit/how-to-apply.html)

The card you use doesn't have to be in your name. The cardholder’s name will appear on the receipt but it does not need to match your application.
